title: Attrition holds at 13.6% while your increment budget shrinks to 8.9%
one_liner: Pay is decelerating but churn is not, so the usual retention lever is being taken away from CHROs precisely when they need it.
source_title: Salary hikes in India to dip to 8.9% in 2026 as attrition stays at 13.6%: Study
source_quote: The report estimates average voluntary turnover at 13.6% next year, broadly in line with last year's levels.
india_relevance_reason: Indian increment cycles are annual, public and peer-benchmarked, so a 0.2pp dip is read by employees as a signal in a way UK merit-pay never is.

title: Manager recognition fell to 15% just as a third of employees plan to leave
one_liner: Retention spend keeps going into rewards platforms while the single strongest driver, manager-led appreciation, is quietly collapsing.
source_title: Employees aren't feeling recognised — and 2026 could see a wave of exits: Report
source_quote: Only 28% of highly appreciated employees are looking for a new job, compared with 71% of undervalued employees.
india_relevance_reason: In India the reporting manager is also the informal career sponsor, so withdrawal of recognition reads as blocked progression, not just low morale.

title: One in nine white-collar hires fails employment verification, not education checks
one_liner: HR teams over-invest in degree verification while the real leak is prior-employment claims, where the discrepancy rate runs nearly three times higher.
source_title: Hiring discrepancies persist in H1 FY26; on-demand workforce faces higher risks: AuthBridge report
source_quote: Among white-collar hires, employment verification emerged as the most impacted category, with a discrepancy rate of 11.15%, followed by address verification at 7.68%.
india_relevance_reason: India's fragmented employment records and the shadow market in fake relieving letters make prior-employment fraud a structural risk no Manchester employer faces at this scale.
cta_text: Free 15-minute review of your current BGV coverage gaps

title: Central labour code rules are notified; your offer letters are now out of date
one_liner: The 8 May 2026 central rules change wage definitions, night-shift consent and contracting paperwork, yet most 500-plus headcount firms have not re-papered anything.
source_title: India – Government of India Notifies Final Rules on Four Labour Codes
source_quote: Employers could review existing policies, contracts and processes to assess compliance with the prescribed rules.
india_relevance_reason: Compliance here is split between central and state notifications, so a Mumbai plant and a Bengaluru office of the same company can sit under different rules on the same day.

title: Fresher hiring intent climbs to 75% while IT quietly steps back to 76%
one_liner: Campus demand is shifting from IT services to retail, e-commerce and manufacturing, which most campus calendars and college relationships were never built for.
source_title: Fresher hiring intent rises to 75%, but IT demand loses ground: Report
source_quote: Seventy-five per cent of the 1,097 employers surveyed by TeamLease EdTech intend to hire freshers between July and December 2026, up from 73% in the first half of the year.
india_relevance_reason: Indian campus hiring runs on Day-0 slotting agreements with colleges, so a sector shift forces renegotiation of institutional relationships, not just job ads.

title: India leads global hiring confidence, but 11% of employers still plan headcount cuts
one_liner: The headline optimism hides a split market: confidence and contraction are happening inside the same quarter and often the same sector.
source_title: India tops global hiring confidence as 65% of employers plan recruitment in Q4 2026
source_quote: Among the 3,055 Indian employers surveyed, 24% expect workforce levels to remain unchanged, while 11% anticipate reducing headcount.
india_relevance_reason: Indian festive-quarter demand and Q3 appraisal cycles collide in Oct-Dec, so workforce plans have to absorb both expansion and exits simultaneously.

title: Diversity hiring grew 21% while overall white-collar hiring cooled
one_liner: Inclusion budgets survived the slowdown, and 18% of those hires are at senior level, which breaks the usual entry-level-only pattern.
source_title: India's Diversity Hiring Surges 21% in May 2026: Report
source_quote: Currently, 18% of diversity-focused hires are at the senior management and leadership level, suggesting that inclusion is becoming a structural priority rather than just an entry-level initiative.
india_relevance_reason: India's female labour force participation drop-off happens at mid-career, so senior diversity hires require re-entry pipelines that Western firms rarely need to build.

title: 20,000 assessments postponed after impersonation: your proctoring is the weak link
one_liner: If a firm with that assessment infrastructure had to halt hiring, mid-size enterprises running unproctored online tests are almost certainly already compromised.
source_title: Infosys postpones hiring exams for 20,000 candidates following impersonation cases
source_quote: Infosys has postponed online assessments and in-person evaluations for more than 20,000 job applicants after detecting multiple instances of impersonation and assessment malpractice during its recruitment process.
india_relevance_reason: India has an organised proxy-interview cottage industry priced per round, which simply does not exist as a commercial service in most Western markets.
cta_text: Ask us for our 6-point proxy-candidate screening checklist

title: Tier-2 capability centre presence jumped 40%, but your comp bands did not follow
one_liner: Enterprises open Indore and Coimbatore sites for cost arbitrage, then lose candidates because pay grids and titles are still written for Bengaluru.
source_title: Jobs in Tier-2 Cities in India: Top Roles, Industries & Growth Trends [2026]
source_quote: Tier-2 city GCC presence has increased by 40% in just a few years, with roles emerging across R&D, AI, software engineering, analytics, shared services, and more.
india_relevance_reason: Tier-2 India offers genuine cost differentials with thin senior talent density, a combination no comparable UK regional market presents.

title: Half of CXO moves involve leaders with under three years in the last role
one_liner: Boards still screen for long tenure as a proxy for stability, while the actual leadership market has repriced around readiness for the next mandate.
source_title: Sapphire Human Capital Decodes The Changing Leadership Landscape In India With CXO Moves Report 2025–26.
source_quote: Nearly 48% of CXO movements involved leaders with 1–3 years in their previous roles, reflecting a more fluid market where relevance and readiness for the next mandate are gaining importance.
india_relevance_reason: Indian promoter-led boards weigh tenure and loyalty far more heavily than plc boards, so this data directly contradicts a deeply held local screening norm.

title: Your 90-day notice period is inflating offer dropouts by a third
one_liner: Long notices are defended as a retention control, but they mainly extend the window in which your accepted offers get counter-offered away.
source_title: Notice Period India: 90-Day Rule Explained [2026]
source_quote: When a company extends an offer to a candidate who has a 90-day notice period, the hiring timeline extends to 3+ months from offer acceptance to the candidate's first day.
india_relevance_reason: 90-day notices are a contractual norm in Indian IT and services with no statutory basis, a lock-in period UK employers would find unenforceable.
cta_text: Get our offer-to-join protection playbook for 90-day notice hires

title: Time-to-hire improved but time-to-productivity did not move at all
one_liner: TA dashboards celebrate a faster funnel while the seat stays empty for another quarter, because notice periods sit outside the metric being measured.
source_title: Time to Hire Benchmarks 2026: What Good Actually Looks Like, by Role and Sector
source_quote: In India a candidate can accept in week one and still be 90 days from a desk, which means your time to hire can improve while time to productivity does not move at all.
india_relevance_reason: The accept-to-join gap is a distinctly Indian metric problem created by long contractual notices, so imported TA benchmarks systematically mislead here.

title: TA headcount is shrinking while requisition volume keeps climbing
one_liner: US recruiter headcount fell for the first time on record. Indian TA teams face the same freeze while GCC req loads in Bengaluru and Hyderabad rise.
source_title: What's Happening to Talent Acquisition Careers? (2026 edition)
source_quote: In 2025, newly released BLS data shows, the number of Human Resources Specialists fell for the first time since the BLS began providing the data in 2012.
india_relevance_reason: Reframes a US BLS headcount statistic as the Indian GCC hiring-load-versus-frozen-TA-headcount squeeze.

title: One disengaged manager can undo an entire quarter of hiring
one_liner: ADP data shows leader engagement decides team engagement. In India the effect peaks right after the appraisal cycle, when regretted exits cluster under specific managers.
source_title: The Leadership Blind Spot Quietly Driving Attrition: 5 Solutions
source_quote: A recent study from ADP found that when a team leader is fully engaged, 65% of their team members are fully engaged, compared to less than 1% of team members when the team leader is not fully engaged.
india_relevance_reason: Ties manager-driven attrition to the Indian appraisal calendar and post-hike resignation spike.

title: A 90-day notice period is not a knowledge transfer plan
one_liner: Institutional knowledge leaves through informal mentoring, not handover documents. India's long notice periods create the illusion of transfer while the exiting employee has already checked out.
source_title: Turnover and How to Avoid Institutional Knowledge Loss
source_quote: Formal training is essential, but informal mentoring is too.
india_relevance_reason: Reframes knowledge loss around India's 60-90 day notice-period culture and its false sense of handover.
cta_text: Free notice-period handover audit for one critical team

title: How you exit people decides who accepts your next offer
one_liner: Survivors judge employers by how leavers were treated. In India that verdict lands on AmbitionBox and Blind within days, shaping offer acceptance for the next two quarters.
source_title: Layoffs on the Rise: 6 Ways to Make Them Easier on Everyone
source_quote: Even better, 65% of employees who survived a layoff and knew their laid-off colleagues got career transition services viewed their employer in a positive light.
india_relevance_reason: Connects layoff conduct to Indian employer-review platforms and downstream offer acceptance rates.

title: Phased exits beat external leadership hires on time to competency
one_liner: Structured mentor-successor overlap cuts time-to-competency sharply. For Indian enterprises, that beats a six-month external leadership search plus a 90-day notice period.
source_title: Flextirement: 5 Keys to Redesign Work to Honor Talent, Experience
source_quote: This structured mentorship framework significantly reduces the time-to-competency for the successor (often by 30-50%) and ensures the successor is not just technically competent but leadership-ready.
india_relevance_reason: Compares succession overlap against the Indian reality of long leadership searches plus long notice periods.

title: One line in your background check consent form is a liability
one_liner: A single disclosure-form footnote cost one US retailer $600,000. Indian employers face the same exposure under the DPDP Act when BGV consent is bundled into the offer letter.
source_title: Background Checks: A $600K FCRA Compliance Mistake
source_quote: Barnes & Noble, for example, paid $600,000 after a single footnote in their disclosure form sparked litigation.
india_relevance_reason: Maps FCRA disclosure risk onto India's DPDP Act consent requirements for background verification.
cta_text: Free BGV consent and DPDP readiness check

title: Cost per hire is the cheapest number in your attrition problem
one_liner: Replacement cost dwarfs cost per hire. Indian CHROs optimise agency fees while a single early exit burns the EPFO onboarding, training and ramp investment twice over.
source_title: Rethinking Recruitment: Building Retention From Day One
source_quote: According to a study by the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM), the average cost-per-hire is around $4,700.
india_relevance_reason: Reframes cost-per-hire benchmarking around Indian ramp-up and statutory onboarding costs lost to early exits.
cta_text: Free true cost-per-hire model for your top three roles

title: Passive onboarding is why your 90-day dropouts keep repeating
one_liner: One-directional onboarding predicts early exits. In India, where offers are held until day one and joiners arrive with competing options, passive week one loses them fast.
source_title: Retention Starts on Day One: Empowering New Hires in Onboarding
source_quote: Onboarding is most effective when it also empowers employees to shape their own adjustment experience.
india_relevance_reason: Links onboarding design to India's offer-shopping and 90-day dropout pattern in high-volume hiring.

title: Global HR platforms break at the India compliance layer first
one_liner: Running people programmes across a dozen countries is structurally different from one country. Indian GCCs discover this when DPDP data residency collides with a global rollout.
source_title: 9 Questions Global HR Leaders Should Ask Before Choosing Employee Recognition Software
source_quote: Running a recognition program for 50,000 people across a dozen countries is a fundamentally different challenge than running one for a single-country team of 500.
india_relevance_reason: Reframes multi-country HR platform selection around Indian DPDP data residency and GCC rollout constraints.

title: AI screening will not fix a hiring process that leaks candidates
one_liner: Automation scales whatever process you already have. Indian enterprises adding AI screening on top of slow panel scheduling just reach the same dropouts faster.
source_title: The Ghost in the ATS: Why AI Won't Save Bad Recruiting (But It Just Might Save Yours)
source_quote: You cannot automate authentic human connection.
india_relevance_reason: Applies the automation critique to Indian panel-scheduling delays that drive time-to-hire and dropouts.

title: AI-written applications have made your first-round interview the real screen
one_liner: Resumes no longer differentiate once LLMs write them. Indian TA teams facing thousands of applications per GCC role must move evidence gathering into the first live conversation.
source_title: The 2026 Talent Acquisition Playbook: Mastering the AI-Human Balance in Recruitment
source_quote: An LLM can write a bullet point, but it cannot authentically fake the passion, the struggle, and the specific granular details of a hard-won victory in a live interview.
india_relevance_reason: Reframes AI-inflated applications around Indian high-volume GCC applicant loads and first-round interview design.

title: Junior attrition tops 22% while your leadership bench barely moves
one_liner: One blended attrition number hides the fact that almost all the churn sits in your first two grades, not across the org.
source_title: Average Attrition Rates Across Indian Industries in 2026: Predictive Retention
source_quote: Junior roles in high-growth sectors exhibit turnover rates exceeding 22%, driven largely by rapid compensation escalation in the external market.
india_relevance_reason: Indian junior-grade pay escalates externally far faster than internal increment cycles allow, a gap UK employers rarely face.

title: Most India GCCs need over 45 days to close a critical role
one_liner: GCC expansion plans assume a talent pipeline the centre has not built; the 45-day mark is where the board timeline quietly slips.
source_title: New GCCs in India: Who Launched, Who's Expanding, and Who's Coming Next (2024-2026)
source_quote: 58% of GCCs in India take more than 45 days to fill critical roles
india_relevance_reason: Bengaluru and Hyderabad now have more GCCs bidding for the same engineers than any single city outside the US.
cta_text: Ask for our 45-day critical-role fill audit for your Bengaluru or Hyderabad centre

title: Offer acceptance fell from 74% to 51% in two years
one_liner: Half your offers now fail to convert, which means half your requisition plan is fiction before the financial year starts.
source_title: Candidate Ghosting in India 2026: Why 76% of Recruiters Are Being Left Behind
source_quote: Offer acceptance fell to 51% in Q2 2025, down from 74% in Q2 2023
india_relevance_reason: Indian candidates routinely hold three live offers through a 90-day notice; a Manchester hire starts in four weeks.

title: Score joining risk the day the offer is accepted, not later
one_liner: Treat the notice period as an active funnel stage with a risk score, or discover the dropout on the joining date.
source_title: Why Candidates Don't Join After Accepting Offers
source_quote: Some recruitment teams now formally score each accepted candidate on signals like notice period length, likelihood of a counter-offer, response speed after the offer, relocation complexity and family decision dependency.
india_relevance_reason: A 90-day Indian notice period gives counter-offers three months to work; most Western markets give them three weeks.
cta_text: Get our joining-risk scorecard template for accepted offers

title: Tier-2 GCC footprint grew 40% while your salary benchmarks stayed metro
one_liner: Enterprises are opening Tier-2 sites but still pricing roles, structuring panels and sourcing as though every hire sits in Bengaluru.
source_title: Jobs in Tier-2 Cities in India: Top Roles, Industries & Growth Trends [2026]
source_quote: Tier-2 city GCC presence has increased by 40% in just a few years, with roles emerging across R&D, AI, software engineering, analytics, shared services, and more.
india_relevance_reason: Coimbatore, Indore and Kochi have real engineering supply at metro-minus cost, a spread no UK region replicates.

title: A 9.1% national hike average is useless for your comp committee
one_liner: The headline increment number spans a three-point sector gap, so benchmarking to the average systematically underpays whichever function you actually need.
source_title: Corporate India to see 9.1% salary hike in 2026 as attrition normalises: Aon survey
source_quote: Real estate and infrastructure companies are expected to offer the highest increments at 10.2%, followed closely by Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) at 10.1%.
india_relevance_reason: Indian increment cycles are annual, public and sector-wide, so a mispriced band is visible to every candidate by April.

title: Your cost per hire is wrong because it counts only agency invoices
one_liner: Recruiter hours and interview panel time are the largest line items in a mid-senior hire and almost nobody books them.
source_title: 15 HR Metrics Every Indian Employer Must Track in 2026 (With Benchmarks and Formulas)
source_quote: Most Indian companies undercount this metric by including only agency fees, missing the significant internal costs of recruiter time, interview panel hours, and job board subscriptions.
india_relevance_reason: Indian panels routinely run four to six rounds with senior engineers, so unbooked interview hours dwarf the agency fee.

title: Fixed-term staff now earn gratuity at one year, not five
one_liner: The labour codes just repriced every project-based and contract-bound role on your books, and most cost models still assume the old five-year rule.
source_title: India's Labor Law Overhaul: Snapshot of Key Changes
source_quote: Employers with significant fixed-term or project-based workforces will need to review staffing models and update cost projections.
india_relevance_reason: Twenty-nine central Acts collapsed into four codes on 21 November 2025; no comparable overhaul exists in the UK.
cta_text: Request a labour-code readiness review of your contract staffing cost model

title: Campus offers convert better outside the metros than inside them
one_liner: Tier-1 institute brand names lose the offer race; smaller-city campuses convert because candidates are not juggling five competing offers.
source_title: Campus Hiring Statistics India 2026: What the Numbers Say
source_quote: Offer-to-join conversion tends to be higher outside the metros, where a strong package means more and candidates are less likely to be juggling five competing offers.
india_relevance_reason: India graduates roughly 1.5 million engineers a year across hundreds of campuses, so tier choice is a live lever, not a formality.

title: CXO searches now collapse at the final slate, not at sourcing
one_liner: The shortage is not candidates. It is outdated success profiles that make the last two names walk away after months of process.
source_title: Solving the Leadership Hiring Crisis: 2026 Challenges and Fastest-Growing Solutions for CXO & Senior Management Recruitment
source_quote: Leadership hiring has become one of the biggest execution risks for organizations heading into 2026.
india_relevance_reason: Indian promoter-led boards often define the CXO role mid-search, which is exactly when a calibrated slate falls apart.

title: Ghost employment: EPFO shows zero contributions for a claimed tenure
one_liner: A whole stretch of a CV can be fabricated and still pass reference checks, because only PF data proves the job existed.
source_title: Moonlighting Detection in India 2026: The Complete EPFO/UAN Verification Guide for HR Leaders
source_quote: The candidate claims to have been employed at a company for a given period, but EPFO shows zero contributions.
india_relevance_reason: The UAN gives Indian employers a government-maintained employment trail that no UK verification process has an equivalent for.

title: One in three new hires exits before day 90 in corporate India
one_liner: A 90-day exit is a hiring and onboarding failure, not an employee failure, and your annual attrition number never shows it.
source_title: Onboarding Programs That Actually Reduce 90-Day Attrition in Indian Companies
source_quote: There is a number most Indian HR leaders know but rarely say out loud: roughly one in three new employees in corporate India exits before their 90th day.
india_relevance_reason: Indian joiners often hold a parallel offer through probation, so week-one ambiguity converts straight into a day-60 resignation.
